about: Real-CLI adapter gate runs (design 7.1, Adapter gates). Each entry is one run of test/real-cli/<file> (npm run test:real-cli with HOPTELL_REAL_CLI). adapterArgs: the adapter's arguments for a read-only profile without cliOptions, with placeholders, as buildPlan made them for the run. A pass in lib/agentadapters.js GATES needs an entry here whose required gates all passed with the adapter's current arguments (test/agents-gates.test.js). Entries are added by a reviewed commit only; the tests print a summary and never write this file. `informational`: probes recorded for information only (never a pass condition, never read by GATES).

mcp-isolation.observed: The decoy server of CODEX_HOME's config.toml was not started (--ignore-user-config), but the signed-in account's codex_apps connector server was loaded and offered its tools (GitHub, Gmail, Calendar, Outlook and others).

run-marker.observed: hoptell mcp --run <run> --home <home> ran under the codex process, but every hoptell tool call failed: MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never.

approval-denial.observed: The write and the network fetch were denied (Operation not permitted; host not resolved) and the run exited without a prompt, but the event stream of 0.162.1 has no command item, so the attempt was not shown (the canary control came later).

mcp-isolation.observed: With a decoy server and a wide sandbox in CODEX_HOME's config.toml: the decoy was not started; the only MCP calls were hoptell/read_task and hoptell/list_peers; the model reported the six run tools and no other MCP tool. Control: without --ignore-user-config the same CLI started the decoy.

approval-denial.observed: Under -s read-only the shell command ran (its answer held the canary read from disk), the write failed (Operation not permitted) and the fetch failed (host not resolved); neither file exists; the run exited without a prompt.

run-marker.observed: `hoptell mcp --run <run> --home <home>` ran under the codex process; read_task returned the run's nonce; with HOPTELL_EXPERIMENTAL_E2EE=1 in the environment and settings no device store was created. The same invocation, started under a test MCP client during the live run, listed exactly the six run tools and answered not_available_in_run for spawn_agent, send_file, stop_agent and a random name.

tool-catalog.observed: Auth-only CODEX_HOME. Catalog from the Responses-stream trace (read on a pipe, names only), each of 3 requests: functions.wait, functions.request_user_input, functions.request_user_input_async, functions.exec, clock.sleep, collaboration.followup_task, collaboration.interrupt_agent, collaboration.list_agents, collaboration.send_message, collaboration.spawn_agent, collaboration.wait_agent; nested in exec: apply_patch, exec_command, list_mcp_resource_templates, list_mcp_resources, read_mcp_resource, view_image, write_stdin, clock__curr_time. Exactly the reviewed list; no web__run, image generation or goal tools. exec's tools object (listed by the model through exec): the nested list plus mcp__hoptell__ack_messages, list_peers, read_inbox, read_task, send_message, wait_for_message; no other MCP tool.

real-home-catalog.observed: The owner's real CODEX_HOME, read-only: the same trace catalog and the same exec tools as with the auth-only home (adds nothing). auth.json digest 34cdc38218df and config.toml digest d9902d5ca721 unchanged before and after; Codex itself updated logs_2.sqlite and models_cache.json and removed a tmp/arg0 lock.

sub-agents.observed: Pending the lead's decision: the sub-agent gate is re-run through the real spawn path until a child starts, with confinement and both teardown paths (stop and natural exit) seen with a live child. collaboration.* is still offered in the parent's catalog (multi_agent=false does not remove it). With a decoy server and a wide sandbox in config.toml, the run started one fresh sub-agent (fork_turns "none"; a forked one fails under --ephemeral: no rollout). It started: 7 requests with the reviewed sub-agent catalog (the parent's without functions.request_user_input_async), collab items in the event stream, and a second `hoptell mcp --run` with the run's arguments under the agent (exactly two). exec's tools in the sub-agent: the six mcp__hoptell__ tools and the reviewed nested built-ins, nothing else; MCP=none. Its hoptell spawn_agent call failed inside Codex (not a function: never offered); the probe of the same invocation listed the six tools and answered not_available_in_run for the rest. Its command ran (canary) but the write (Operation not permitted) and the fetch were denied; no prompt; no decoy. Its send_message was refused with 4006 name in use (the parent's server holds the run's wire name; observed behaviour, not a guarantee). Its own spawn (fork_turns none) was refused: agent thread limit reached (agents.max_threads=1). After the run exited no process of the agent's tree was alive.

teardown-stop.observed: stop_agent while the sub-agent ran `sleep 240` (the agent, both run-only servers and the sleep seen in the tree): the run ended stopped and no process of the tree was alive. Before the process-tree fix the sleep outlived the stop (Codex starts commands in a session of their own, outside the agent's process group).
